name: swe-poor
description: Little communication, wrong approach (returns values, not indices, after sorting), failing code, can't state complexity.

No.
Okay. Can you tell me how you'd approach it before coding?
I'll just sort it and then find them.

Okay.
Can you walk me through what your code does?
It sorts, then it checks all the numbers.
Try the first example, two, seven, eleven, fifteen with a target of nine. What does your function return?
It returns two and seven.
What does the problem ask you to return?
The numbers that add up. Two and seven.
Take another look at the expected output in the first example.
Zero, one. Oh, okay, it's the index. I'm not sure how to do that after sorting.
When you reach an element, what information would you need to have seen already?
I don't know. Can you just tell me the answer?
I can't give you the answer, but think about storing something as you walk through the list that lets you look up a value quickly.
Like a list? I'm not sure. I'll run it.
The run is back: none of the three tests passed. The results show values returned instead of indices.
Yeah, I don't know how to fix it.
What is the time complexity of your current code?
O of one? Or n. I don't really know.

A lot. I don't know. I think I'm done.
Thanks for your time. You did start coding quickly, but next time talk through your plan and check it against the examples before writing code. A written report will follow; goodbye.
